To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structures of the orthorhombically crystallized A2U and of a complex of A2U with a hyalinedroplet inducer have been solved and refined at 2.5 and 2.9 angstrom resolution, respectively.

A2U and MUP, which share 80% sequence identity, differ in the shape of their ligand-binding cavities and that this is the reason why A2U is a more sensitive indicator of the nephrotoxic potential of a wide variety of chemicals than MUP.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the major urinary proteins (MUPs) in the rat and mouse.
the structure and function of A2U.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of hyaline-d roplet nephropathy in male rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of A2U and the structure of the A2U/DLO complex have provided a molecular explanation of the mechanism of action of DLO and of other hyaline droplets.
DLO is bound in a pocket in A2U which is lined by the hydrophobic side chains of Leu(8), Phe(10), Val(13), Phe(14), Val(17) and Phe(18) and by the main-chain atoms of residues 9-11 and 13-18.
DLO binds to A2U in the same way as it does to MUP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A2U-DLO complex is the first structure of an endogenous protein complex which causes renal carcinogenesis in a mammal.
the binding site of A2U is a deep, oval, hydrophobic depression in which DLO fits snugly.
the structure of A2U is a consequence of a long evolutionary process of adaptation to a specific function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of a ligand to A2U induces significant conformational changes in the protein.
the binding of DLO to A2U is a consequence of the unique structure of the cavity.
the cavity in A2U has a unique structure and is a good fit for a wide range of small hydrophobic molecules.
